newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government agrees 1997 budget review.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government agrees 1997 budget review.

text.p: The Belgian government on Saturday decided on a package of spending cuts and tax rises to keep the 1997 budget on target for European monetary union, Belgian media said.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's spokeswoman declined to confirm an agreement had been reached and said talks would continue through the weekend.

BRTN radio said ministers had decided on 12 billion francs ($342 million) of new austerity measures to make sure the 1997 state deficit remains on target to fall to 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), from 3.4 percent in 1996.

The 1997 budget is crucial for Belgium, as it will determine whether the country qualifies to join the single currency in 1999. It was drawn up in October 1996 and contained austerity measures worth 80 billion francs.

But an estimated 25 billion franc shortfall in 1997 tax receipts, only partly compensated by 10 billion francs of budget savings due to low interest rates, has forced the government to take corrective measures during its annual spring budget review.
As expected, none of the measures targeted consumers.

"We did not have to take any measures which people will feel directly," Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte told VTM television at the entrance of Val Duchesse, a chateau south of Brussels where the ministers have gathered for the weekend.
Belgian media said the measures include a 1.5 billion franc tax on the electricity sector and a two billion franc turnover tax on the pharmaceutical industry.

New income tax prepayments for the self employed must raise one billion francs and sharper control on value added tax-evasion two billion francs. Several ministries, including defence and development cooperation, will have their budgets cut by three to four billion francs.

Talks on the budget and on a review of the centre-left government's policy agreement will continue all weekend and Monday. On Sunday, talks will focus on the reform of the justice system and the fight against unemployment.
Dehaene is set to address parliament about the budget and the updated government agreement on Tuesday. $1 = 34.81 Belgian francs
